name: Kha'Zix, Voidreaver
howItPlays: You send units into fights to win combats and bank experience on Kha'Zix, then spend it to make an ally hit harder or pull a beat-up unit home to base before it can be finished off. You mix cheap units with hidden and surprise effects alongside a few bigger threats that take over once the game reaches its middle turns.
whyYou: You like games where every fight matters and you keep deciding whether to press an advantage or pull a hurt unit to safety. You enjoy holding a few surprises in reserve and sensing when the opponent is about to overextend. If you would rather build a strong turn five or six out of small wins than gamble everything early, Kha'Zix suits you.
ratingNotes:
pace 5: riftbound.gg calls Kha'Zix a midrange plan built around 4-5 cost cards after an early combat-focused setup, and hextechanalytics separately calls the speed 'medium pace that requires setup and planning,' so neither source reads it as a rush.
stance 6: hextechanalytics says Kha'Zix is 'primarily proactive,' manipulating the battlefield 'on your own turn' rather than waiting to react, while riftbound.gg describes a more even mix of developing and reacting through Ambush; splitting the difference lands just proactive of center.
complexity 7: hextechanalytics calls it high complexity, since 'those choices compete for the same Legend activation,' forcing a pick between a stronger board or a unit brought home safely each turn; riftbound.gg calls it only moderately intricate, so this leans toward the higher read.
variance 6.5: both sources agree on moderate-to-high, tied to drawing the right movement pieces (Void Assault, Faefolk per hextechanalytics) and to early unit survival (per riftbound.gg).
Legend ability: gain 1 XP on winning a combat; spend 1 XP and exhaust to buff a unit; spend 2 XP and exhaust to move an exhausted friendly unit from a battlefield back to base.
Confidence: high. Two independent guides read in full (riftbound.gg, hextechanalytics.com), both landing on a Midrange read, though they disagree slightly on how proactive versus reactive the deck feels; the seed had this Legend as Aggro, which neither source supports, so the archetype change is worth a second look.
